category: sandbox (hosted router over multiple sandbox providers)
tier: Pay as you go, USD 5 free credit

free_tier.stated: USD 5 in free compute credit to start, with no provider account needed; credit is spent at the listed per-provider compute rates and a 5% platform fee applies when buying more credit
free_tier.notes: the free credit is USD 5 and the bill is drawn from the organization's ComputeSDK balance at the provider's rate; the router does not set a single price of its own, the per-provider table does

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a sandbox session, not a stored object

retention.stated: a sandbox keeps running until the user destroys it or its lifetime expires; closing the terminal or disconnecting a preview does not destroy it, and sandbox and Actions rates may differ

egress.terms: no egress price is published on the read pages; a quote through the routing endpoint reports the provider, region and prepaid credit balance before a sandbox is created

interface_detail: a REST API at https://platform.computesdk.com/api/v1 with an organization API key or OAuth token, a TypeScript SDK that includes the router, the compute CLI, and a remote MCP server
tooling: npm install computesdk for the SDK, npm install @computesdk/cli or curl -fsSL https://computesdk.com/install | sh for the CLI, an org API key from Settings, or the remote MCP server with OAuth
chaining: one integration routes across many sandbox providers, with a fallback order and a choice of provider per run; managed compute spends ComputeSDK credit with no provider account, while BYOK lets a provider bill its own usage directly

limits.value: USD 5 free compute credit at signup, then credits bought with a 5% platform fee, spent at per-provider hourly rates
a sandbox runs until destroyed or its lifetime expires; the rate table lists per-hour prices and billing increments where the provider publishes them

binding_note: the USD 5 credit is what a new user spends first; there is no router-wide concurrency or request ceiling on the read pages, and the per-provider rates determine how long the credit lasts

identity_cost.detail: the signup page asks for a name, an organization, an email address and a password, and offers Continue with Google or Continue with GitHub; the CLI browser login opens the same flow and saves the session locally. The free credit needs no provider account and no payment method is shown before credit is used.

reliability_note: the platform does not charge the 5% fee again on each usage charge; the displayed rate is normalized per hour for comparison and the billing increment is listed separately where the provider publishes one, so short-lived sandboxes can cost a different effective rate
confidence_note: the free credit, fee, rate table and signup fields are quoted from first-party pages read on 2026-11-25; the signup and console are behind a login wall, so the signup fields were read from a direct fetch of the public signup page, and no sandbox was created

notes: A hosted router over many sandbox providers rather than a single sandbox vendor: USD 5 of free compute credit at signup, a 5% fee only when buying more credit, and per-provider rates charged from the organization's balance. The per-provider table lists a 2 vCPU and 4 GB sandbox from USD 0.00604 per hour (agent37) to USD 0.3408 per hour (vercel medium); the operator list's USD 0.31 per hour for 'Sandbox Router' is not a router-wide rate on any page read, so the record states the published per-provider rates instead. The self-hosted SDK libraries are optional clients of this hosted service and come after it, not in its place.

shape.note: the router offers many provider sizes; the per-provider rate table is the source of shape and price

extras.billing_model: prepaid credits spent at per-provider rates, 5% fee on credit purchases
extras.term: on demand; a sandbox runs until destroyed or its lifetime expires
extras.price_arithmetic: USD 5 free credit; 5% fee on purchases; example 2 vCPU / 4 GB rates in the published table are USD 0.00604/h (agent37) and USD 0.3408/h (vercel medium)

session_cap.note: lifetime is set per sandbox; billing increment is listed per provider where available

limits_note: Rates in the table are normalized to USD per hour for comparison; each row lists a billing increment when available, and most rows read 'Not specified'. A quote does not reserve capacity, and being listed in the catalog or benchmarks does not grant access to a provider account.
